solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bishop leading one religious group split down the middle

indicators.note: leading means the bishop's letter comes at the front of what follows

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the Roman numeral for one
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A bishop heads a congregation that has split into two factions.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal halves, the verb behind dividing something centrally.

clue.text: Primate holding former president dear

parts.note: Bush is the name of two former US presidents
baby is a term of endearment, like dear

explanation.surface: An ape holds an affectionate ex-president.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal African primate with huge eyes.

clue.text: In this heat, helmet's put back in case

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In hot weather, the helmet is stored away again in its box.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a sword is to return it to its scabbard.

clue.text: Equipment for filming canoeist, initially, in river sequence

indicators.note: in means the canoeist's initial is placed within the river-and-sequence string

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
an order is a sequence

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of canoeist is used

explanation.surface: Kit for recording a canoeist paddling a run of rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A camcorder is a portable video camera with a built-in recorder.

clue.text: Revolutionary respects some of the trappings of monarchy

definitions.text: some of the trappings of monarchy

indicators.note: something revolutionary overturns the existing order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary pays grudging respect to certain royal regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial staffs carried by kings and queens are among the regalia symbolising royal power.

clue.text: In line with right policies? Vice versa — only changing over time

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters stretch over the T
changing means the letters of these words switch places

explanation.surface: A political pundit says right-wing policy has flipped completely over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on Conservative, the British right-wing party; the adverb usually means cautiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a Tory, right-of-centre manner is a punning reading of this adverb meaning cautiously.

clue.text: It needs copy to fill page, right?

definitions.text: It needs copy to fill page, right?

indicators.note: to fill means the copy word goes into the space between the other letters

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: An editor checks that a newspaper needs articles to fill its pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper must have journalists' copy to fill its pages, which is the whole clue's reading.

clue.text: Get revenge, having overturned monarch fairly

indicators.note: overturned means the monarch's letters are turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
quite means fairly, as in quite good

explanation.surface: Taking revenge after toppling a king reasonably fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay, here in the sense of retaliating for a wrong.

clue.text: Vehicle to bump off, as you can hear

indicators.note: as you can hear means the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: to bump off is to kill, to slay

explanation.surface: A car used to murder someone, as you can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by horses or reindeer over snow.

clue.text: Pursue progress with reform in these

definitions.text: Pursue progress with reform in these

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Campaigners lobby for social progress through reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobbying organisations campaign to change policy, which the whole clue describes them doing.

clue.text: Pressing need in small club without a lot of players

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the small club wraps round the players

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: A tiny club short of members urgently needs something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' is about ironing clothes, not urgency.
explanation.definitionFit: This household appliance is what you need for ironing creases out of garments.

clue.text: Annoyed reaction heard in summit, or just a short-term view?

indicators.note: heard means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a grumpy outburst came from a mountaintop or a brief glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sounds like both 'peak' (summit) and 'peek' (a short-term view, a quick look), so the clue offers two words it is heard as.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a fit of resentment or irritation, typically at a slight to one's pride.

clue.text: Junior hotel worker, yet getting a lot

parts.note: yet and but both mean however
tons is informal for a lot

explanation.surface: A young hotel employee is nonetheless earning plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is an old nickname for a page or bellboy, from the rows of buttons on the uniform.

clue.text: Sinful, pocketing a piece of jewelry

indicators.note: pocketing means the sinful word holds the A inside it

parts.note: erring means going astray morally, sinning

explanation.surface: A wicked person slips a jewel into their pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament worn on the ear lobe is a common item of jewellery.

clue.text: Book studied to make money

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Someone studies a book in order to earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for cash, as in earning a crust.

clue.text: Lacking experience, and prosaic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not versed in something, inexperienced
second meaning, playful: written in prose, so not put into verse

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading: un-versed, not in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Unversed means unskilled or unfamiliar with a subject, and punningly means not rendered as poetry.

clue.text: Tracing carburettor part for vehicle often off the road

indicators.note: part means the answer is a portion of the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A mechanic traces a carburettor fault in an off-road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorsport car competes on circuits and tracks rather than public highways.

clue.text: Temperature right in part of Spain for this herb

indicators.note: in means the R is set inside the Spanish region

parts.note: Aragon is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: The warmth in a Spanish region suits this herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic plant whose leaves flavour sauces such as béarnaise.

clue.text: Prop finally dropped before big match — least effective as line-out jumper?

indicators.note: before places the shortened prop ahead of the match
finally dropped means the last letter of the prop word is removed

parts.note: to shore up is to prop, and a shore is a prop or support
a test is a major international match in rugby or cricket

explanation.surface: In rugby, a prop forward is left out ahead of a test, being poor at jumping in line-outs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' looks like the rugby forward but is a support; in rugby a line-out is where players leap to catch a throw-in, so height matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest player would be worst at leaping for the ball when it is thrown in from touch.

clue.text: Artist making name in sport

indicators.note: in means the N goes inside the sport

parts.note: hockey is a sport

explanation.surface: A painter makes his name in a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: David Hockney is a celebrated English painter, known for his swimming-pool pictures.

clue.text: Constable and another artist needed source of oil

parts.note: a constable is a policeman, a cop
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: John Constable and a fellow painter needed oil paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable reads as the painter, which makes 'another artist' natural; here he is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, from which coconut oil is pressed.

clue.text: Quietly urging action that'll stabilise costs

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly
egging on is urging

explanation.surface: Softly encouraging a measure to hold prices steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegging prices means fixing them at a set level to keep them steady.

clue.text: Understand female cutting party short

indicators.note: cutting with short means trimming the party word, so its final letter goes
short means the last letter of the party is dropped

parts.note: an at-home is a party held in one's own house

explanation.surface: Getting to grips with a woman who leaves a party early.
explanation.walkthrough: An at-home is an old-fashioned name for a reception given in one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, comprehending it.

clue.text: Accountant returned and caught employer who raises charges?

indicators.note: returned means the accountant's letters are read backwards

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: An accountant came back and caught out a boss who raises prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises charges' suggests prices; it means bringing criminal charges.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is the person who levels an accusation of wrongdoing against someone.

clue.text: With less confidence in company, cast going on short English run

indicators.note: going on means the following letters are added after

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast
E is the short form of English
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A timid actor in a theatre company, cast in a short English run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' and 'cast' and 'run' all suggest a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shyer is more bashful and diffident when among other people.

clue.text: Cook raving about Eastern condiment

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the E
to cook is to falsify or doctor, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef ranting about an Oriental seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a noun for a chef; it is the instruction to rearrange RAVING, and that jumble goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid used as a seasoning or dressing at table.

clue.text: Extremes of honesty coming in useful

indicators.note: coming in means the joining word that links the two extreme letters sits between them
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here the two ends of honesty

parts.note: the setter reads 'Extremes of honesty' as the two end letters joined by the word that pairs them, so this little link stands for that joining word

explanation.surface: Being thoroughly honest proves useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'honesty' are H and Y; read out as a pair, they are 'H and Y', and that 'and' coming in between them spells the answer. The joining word comes from the reading, not from any clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is convenient and practical, ready to serve a purpose.

clue.text: No luck in unusually good opening

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Without luck, someone gets an unexpectedly favourable start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' is a verb sense here, not a noun: rearranging NOLUCKIN gives UNLOCKIN, and G finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlocking a door or box is the act of opening it.

clue.text: City official long ago trapped by crowd? Not him

indicators.note: trapped by means the time word sits inside the crowd word

parts.note: a mass is a crowd
yore means time long past

explanation.surface: A municipal dignitary from olden days is hemmed in by a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not him' says the official is a woman: the female counterpart of a mayor, or a mayor's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoress is a female mayor or the wife of a mayor, a civic office holder.

clue.text: Heads off for big gin, for a start

indicators.note: heads off means each of the three words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone orders a large gin to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading 'for', 'big' and 'gin' leaves OR, IG and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point where something begins, its source or beginning.
